ui.existing_rank: Your existing rotation ranks {{rank}} of {{n}} candidate rotations on your priorities.
ui.gl_et0_def: Water lost to the air from soil and plants. It rises with heat, sun and wind and sets how much water crops need.
ui.gl_ndvi_def: A satellite greenness index. Low values on a field suggest bare soil or stressed crops.
ui.gl_sat_def: Satellites see large areas often but coarsely; ground measurements are precise for one spot. Using both is better than either alone.
ui.gl_sma_def: How much wetter or drier the soil is than usual for that time of year.
ui.gl_wb_def: Water in (rain, irrigation) minus water out (evaporation, plant use, drainage) equals the change in soil storage.
ui.heatmap_sub: Simulated moisture, organic matter, pH, and salinity across horizons.
ui.layers_note: Layer names come from the computed texture. “Low” means estimated, not measured.
ui.lookup_summary: mean max {{tmax}} °C · {{rain}} mm rain/yr · ET0 {{et0}} mm/yr
ui.map_hint: Click the map to place your field.
ui.map_label: Map: click to place your field
ui.nasa_note: Satellite data describes regions (kilometres), not a single field. It is combined with local soil information and your own observations.
ui.ndvi_basis_pixel: Single 500 m pixel at the site
ui.ndvi_basis_regional: Regional median (~15 km box, 500 m pixels) - not the field
ui.ndvi_not_classified: Crop and fallow periods are not separated enough to classify, so only the observed curve is shown.
ui.no_overlap: No overlapping days between the observations and the simulation, so no statistics are shown.
ui.no_webgl: The 3D view is not available on this device. All results are shown in the text and charts.
ui.or_custom_field: Click anywhere on the map to place your field and tune its soil and crop history:

ui.smap_depth: SMAP represents about the top 5 cm of soil; the model's top layer is 0–20 cm.

ui.timeline_label: Timeline of seasons, rain, ET0 and soil moisture
ui.usda_triangle_sub: Numbers are layers; dashed line traces texture variation with depth.

landing.battlefield_title: The Agri-Tech Battlefield: Space vs Under the Soil
landing.battlefield_subtitle: Satellites see everything from 700 km above. Soil physics governs root survival. Our engine bridges both.
landing.space_caveat: Limitation: Satellites cannot measure compaction, deep root water uptake, or hardpans under the surface.
landing.soil_caveat: Limitation: Ground samples are localized; without climate telemetry, weather volatility breaks traditional planning.
landing.hybrid_bridge_title: The Hybrid Advantage: Physics-Informed Adaptive Rotations
landing.hybrid_bridge_desc: By fusing daily NASA climate observations with multi-layer soil hydrology (Saxton-Rawls & FAO-56), Journey into the Soil gives Egyptian farmers resilient rotation advice that protects root zones from salt accumulation.
landing.crop_talk_title: Crop Talk: Plant a Question, Grow an Answer
landing.cropy_summary: Cropy can answer questions and talk about anything related to the simulation, root-zone hydrology, or rotation recommendations.
landing.cropy_meta: Calibrated with Egypt SoilGrids & NASA Data
landing.grounded_note: Grounded on FAO-56 and NASA POWER stream
landing.advisory_note: Advisory note: Verify with local drainage conditions
landing.map_subtitle: Interactive agricultural relief map highlighting 27 calibrated Egyptian governorates with NASA POWER telemetry and SoilGrids hydrology.
landing.hero_subtitle: Adaptive crop rotation & root-zone hydrological simulation bridging NASA Earth observations with real soil physical strata.
landing.nasa_modal_title: NASA Satellite Telemetry vs Ground Sensors
landing.nasa_modal_sub: Cross-validation between satellite observation streams and underground root-zone physics.
landing.param_meteomatics: Meteomatics High-Res Downscaled Soil & Weather (NASA SRTM 90m)
landing.report_meta: Calibrated via NASA POWER & Egypt SoilGrids · Beneficiary:
landing.rot_y1_desc: Chickpea restores root-zone nitrogen (45 kg N/ha) and buffers against irrigation salts under winter rain flush.
landing.rot_y2_desc: Highest osmotic tolerance; reduces summer irrigation water demand by 28% while extracting deep moisture.
landing.rot_y3_desc: Deep taproots break subsoil hardpan crust; incorporates organic green manure before next cereal cycle.
landing.lf_desc: Computed via FAO-56 Dual Kc Water Balance to prevent root-zone sodium accumulation.
landing.report_disclaimer: Advisory decision-support only. NASA Space Apps 2026 'Field Shift'. Does not replace local soil laboratory testing or agronomist field judgment. No fertilizer rates or yield guarantees provided.
landing.workflow_subtitle: From satellite orbits to microscopic soil pores, our three-tier engine translates raw space data into actionable rotation plans.
landing.step1_desc: Daily NASA POWER solar irradiance, GPM IMERG rainfall, and SMAP surface moisture stream directly into the local microclimate profile.
landing.step2_desc: Saxton-Rawls pedotransfer functions calculate saturation, field capacity, wilting point, and vertical solute salt transport across 4 horizons.
landing.step3_desc: FAO-56 dual crop coefficient water balances rank seasonal succession candidates to protect soil biology and conserve scarce canal water.
ui.wizard_lab_data_sub: Leave blank to use calibrated regional defaults
ui.texture_sand_desc: Fast drainage, low water holding (Desert & New Lands).
ui.texture_sandy_loam_desc: Good aeration with moderate retention (Nubaria region).
ui.texture_loam_desc: Balanced silt, sand & clay (Central Nile Delta alluvial).
ui.texture_silt_loam_desc: High water capacity, fine Nile silts (Upper Egypt).
ui.texture_clay_desc: Dense, prone to waterlogging & salt (Northern Delta).
